title: throttLL'eM: Predictive GPU Throttling for Energy-Efficient LLM Inference Serving
summary_zh: throttLL'eM（Kakolyris 等）建立一個迭代級效能預測器（R² > 0.97），以選定能在滿足 SLO 下節省能源的 DVFS／時脈設定。它以記分板分析式投影未來的 KV 快取占用與批次大小（誤差 2.26%／0.19%），餵入梯度提升樹模型 M(E,KV,B,F) 預測吞吐，再以二分搜尋找出滿足端到端與 token 間期限的最低 GPU 頻率，並結合張量並行實例自動擴縮。相對 NVIDIA Triton，能耗最多下降 43.8%、能效提升至少 1.71×。對我們而言，這是論點的反面：時脈是系統「設定」並作為已知輸入餵入的旋鈕；我們則預測控制器隨輸入負載上升而「非自願取走」的時脈，作為界定我們新穎性的關鍵分界。
summary_en: throttLL'eM (Kakolyris et al.) builds an iteration-level performance predictor (R² > 0.97) to choose a DVFS/clock setting that saves energy while meeting SLOs. A scoreboard analytically projects future KV-cache usage and batch size (2.26%/0.19% error), feeding a gradient-boosted tree M(E,KV,B,F) that predicts throughput; a per-iteration binary search then finds the lowest GPU frequency satisfying the end-to-end and per-token deadlines, combined with tensor-parallel instance autoscaling. Against NVIDIA Triton it cuts energy by up to 43.8% and improves efficiency by at least 1.71×. For us this is the inverse of our thesis: the clock is a knob the system sets and feeds in as a known input, whereas we predict the clock the controller involuntarily takes away as a function of input load — the key delimiter of our novelty.
